events.text: The Gathering of the Isle Young is called on the Isle of the Jade Court, and every faction sends its brightest. The bouts are fought on a terrace with no railing, over a fall of ten thousand li. The crowd is immortals who have seen everything, and are bored by most of it.

choices.text: Step onto the terrace

roll.foeName: A bright one of the Gathering

ok.log: You win three bouts and the bored immortals stop being bored. Your name is written on the Court's board in jade ink.

fail.log: You go over the railing that is not there, and catch yourself on the cloud sea. The crowd applauds the recovery.

choices.text: Watch, and learn three forms

effects.log: You watch every bout and steal three forms clean. Nobody minds: up here, that is what watching is for.

events.text: The Games of the Novice Spirits open in the hall of the Heavenly Court: young gods, newly made, testing their domains against each other while the old gods take notes. {b10_pantheon} has asked you to sponsor a champion.

choices.text: Sponsor a young god of your domain

effects.log: Your young god wins two rounds and loses the third with great dignity. {b10_pantheon} is pleased, and says so in public.

choices.text: Judge a round yourself

effects.log: You judge fairly, which surprises everyone. Two young gods will remember you for it, one kindly.

events.text: The Games of the Kingdoms are called early this year, and every inn of {pw_kingdom} is full of young fighters stretching in the courtyards. A notice on the gate says the first rounds are open to all comers, three days from now.

choices.text: Enter the first rounds

roll.foeName: A young fighter of the Games

ok.log: You win four bouts in three days and your name goes up on the board in red paint. People point at you in the street.

fail.log: You lose in the third bout to someone who bows very politely afterwards. The crowd claps for you anyway.

choices.text: Run a stall of liniment for the bruised

effects.log: By the second day you have sold out twice. Everyone in the Games knows your name, though not for fighting.

events.text: Black clouds boil up from the Demon Realm under the isles. The Celestial Ministries ring every bell on the Ninth Stair and call immortals to the watch-terraces. Your neighbour, an alchemist who has not left their furnace in four hundred years, is already putting on armour.

choices.text: Stand the watch on the lowest terrace

ok.log: The black tide breaks on your terrace and goes back down. The marshals of the Ministries write your name in the book of the watch.

fail.log: The tide nearly takes the terrace. You hold, barely, and the marshals carry you up the stair afterwards.

choices.text: Brew for the watch all night

effects.log: You and the alchemist brew until dawn. Every immortal on the terraces drinks something of yours.

events.text: A fallen god has raised a host of the forsaken at the edge of the domains, and the shrines of the borders are going dark one by one. The pantheons are calling every god to the border. {b10_domain} is not far from it.

choices.text: Lead your worshippers' prayers to the border

ok.log: The forsaken break on the light of a thousand prayers. The border shrines light again, and their keepers carve your name.

fail.log: The host comes through. You drive it back in the end, at a cost the border will remember.

choices.text: Shelter the border's worshippers in your domain

effects.log: They come in their thousands. You make room. Some of them never leave, and pray to you now.

events.text: The Shadow Lodges come out of the inns all at once in the river towns of {pw_kingdom}. The Wardens of the roads call for volunteers to hold the ferries. Old people bar their doors and tell the children about the last time.

choices.text: Hold a ferry with the Wardens

ok.log: Your ferry holds all night. In the morning the Wardens give you a grey sash and a nod, which is a great deal from a Warden.

fail.log: They take the ferry. You get everyone off first, and swim for it.

choices.text: Hide the stallholders' children

effects.log: You hide eleven children in a cellar until it is over. Eleven families will never let you pay for bread again.

events.text: Pilgrims from the world below have climbed the long stair to the edge of the clouds, as they do once a generation, and stand there with incense, looking up. They cannot see the isles. They pray anyway.

choices.text: Go down to the edge and let them see you

effects.log: You stand at the cloud's edge until they see you. Some of them weep. One old man just laughs and laughs.

choices.text: Send a rain of peach blossom down

effects.log: It snows peach blossom on the long stair for an hour. They will tell it for a hundred years.

events.text: Your believers keep their festival: from every corner of {b10_domain} they walk to your oldest shrine with lamps, singing songs whose words have changed so much you hardly know them. This year there are more of them than last.

choices.text: Walk among them unseen

effects.log: You walk all night among the lamps. An old woman offers you her cake, as she would any stranger. You eat it.

choices.text: Answer every prayer at the shrine

effects.log: By dawn the shrine is warm as a hearth, and so are you.

events.text: The pilgrims of {pw_kingdom} are walking the old roads to the temples of the god who made this world. They do not know that the god was once a person very like you. Some of them are singing.

choices.text: Walk with them a day

effects.log: You walk a day with them and learn their songs. One of them is about you, more or less.

choices.text: Carry water to the pilgrims

effects.log: You carry water all day. Your shoulders ache and every pilgrim on the road knows your face.

events.text: The Nine Clouds Palace holds its fair of a hundred furnaces on a cloud that never rains. Pill-masters of every isle bring their best, and the air is green with smoke and loud with arguments about honey.

choices.text: Enter a pill of your own

ok.log: Your pill takes third place and a Nine Clouds elder asks for your recipe, which you refuse, which they respect.

fail.log: Your pill takes no place, but the elder who tasted it stops coughing for a week.

choices.text: Buy a furnace master's notes

effects.log: You trade spirit stones for a furnace master's notes, half of which are in a code you will spend a decade on.

events.text: Saengmo, Mother of Seeds, opens her hall for the brewing of the seed pills, and gods of every pantheon come to watch the old goddess work. She hands you a pestle without looking up.

choices.text: Grind for Saengmo all day

effects.log: You grind until your arms ache. At dusk Saengmo tastes the powder and says, "Again tomorrow." From her, that is a hymn.

choices.text: Trade a blessing for one seed pill

effects.log: Saengmo takes your blessing and gives you a seed pill the size of a lentil, warm as a heartbeat.

events.text: The healers of {pw_kingdom} gather in one market town for their fair. The air is green with smoke, the streets smell of bitter roots, and every second stall promises to cure everything.

choices.text: Enter a remedy of your own

ok.log: Your remedy wins a ribbon and three healers ask how you did it. You tell them. They do not believe you.

fail.log: Your remedy cures nothing, but it tastes better than anyone else's, which wins you friends.

choices.text: Buy a cheap stall-keeper's recipe book

effects.log: Most of it is nonsense. One page is not.

events.text: The Red Thread Season comes to the isles: every immortal house counts its unmatched, and the matchmakers of the Peach Isles fly from terrace to terrace with lists that are thousands of years long.

choices.text: Let a matchmaker read your thread

effects.log: The matchmaker reads your thread for an hour and says only, "Interesting." Three invitations arrive the next day.

choices.text: Help two shy immortals meet

effects.log: They have been neighbours for six hundred years and never spoken. They speak now. You are invited to the bond-feast.

events.text: The pantheons are arranging bonds between domains: every feast of the heavens is a negotiation, and two gods of {b10_pantheon} have asked whether you might be persuaded to attend one.

choices.text: Attend, and be charming

effects.log: You are very charming. A domain's god sends you a gift the next day with no note, which in the heavens is a note.

choices.text: Attend, and broker a match for two others

effects.log: You broker a bond between two domains at war for an age. The war ends at the feast.

events.text: The great houses of {pw_kingdom} are arranging marriages, and every feast is an audition. A matchmaker with a very long list has knocked on your door three times this week.

choices.text: Let the matchmaker in

effects.log: The matchmaker talks for two hours and leaves with a list of names and your shoe size. Invitations begin.

choices.text: Help a friend court someone

effects.log: Your friend is hopeless. You are not. The wedding is in spring.

events.text: The Celestial Ministries hold their examinations for clerks of the isles: ten thousand questions on precedence, ten thousand more on law, one essay on the nature of order. Candidates fly in with ink-stained sleeves.

choices.text: Sit the examination

ok.log: You place high enough that a minister sends you a scroll of congratulation and a job offer you decline.

fail.log: You fail on precedence, which everyone does. Your essay is pinned to a wall anyway.

choices.text: Tutor a nervous candidate

effects.log: Your candidate passes. You learn more about the law of the isles teaching it than you ever did reading it.

events.text: The Heavenly Court examines its new judges: young gods set to judge the transgressions of older ones, with the whole Court watching. You have been asked to set one question.

choices.text: Set a hard question about mercy

effects.log: Nobody answers it well. One young god answers it honestly, and the Court remembers that answer for an age.

choices.text: Set a fair question about law

effects.log: Every candidate answers it well, and the Court thanks you for an examination that ended on time.

events.text: The kingdoms of {pw_world} are choosing their clerks this season. Candidates crowd the roads to the capital of {pw_kingdom} with ink-stained fingers, and the lists go up at the end of the season.

choices.text: Sit the clerks' examination

ok.log: Your name is on the list in the second row. A clerk of the king asks to see your hand.

fail.log: Your name is not on the list. Your essay, somehow, is quoted in a tavern a month later.

choices.text: Sell ink and lamp-oil to the candidates

effects.log: You sell out every day. The candidates who pass remember who sold them ink.

events.text: Cloud-sea beasts come in from the outer mist every year at this time: great flat whales of cloud, serpents of thunder, cranes as big as houses. The factions hunt them for sport, and the beasts hunt the hunters.

choices.text: Hunt a thunder serpent

ok.log: You bring down a thunder serpent over the outer isles. Its scales are worth a fortune in spirit stones.

fail.log: The serpent brings you down instead, into the mist, and lets you go. Beasts have a sense of humour.

choices.text: Ride a cloud whale instead of hunting it

effects.log: You ride it for three days, far out over the mist, and come back with nothing but a story.

events.text: Horang, Lord of the Wild, opens the hunting grounds of the Beasts domain to every god for one season. The beasts there are older than temples, and the rule is Horang's: what you take, you must name.

choices.text: Hunt a beast older than temples

ok.log: You take it, and name it, and Horang nods, which is more than most gods get.

fail.log: It takes a piece of your divine body and walks off. Horang laughs for a long time.

choices.text: Name a beast without taking it

effects.log: You give it a name and let it go. Horang says that counts double, and gives you a tooth.

events.text: The hunting grounds of {pw_kingdom} open in autumn, and beasts come down from the high hills. So do the hunters, with their dogs, their horns and their arguments.

choices.text: Hunt the great stag of the hills

ok.log: You bring it down with one clean strike. Your name is toasted at every fire.

fail.log: The stag outruns you all day. You come back with a rabbit and a story.

choices.text: Hunt quietly for the kitchens

effects.log: You bring back enough for three kitchens and no glory at all. The cooks love you.

events.text: A sealed isle rises out of the cloud sea with its gate open, as it does once in a thousand years. Its grottoes breathe again. Every faction sends a party, and every party pretends not to see the others.

choices.text: Go in through the gate

ok.log: In a grotto nobody has entered since the isles were young you find a jade slip of an immortal method, and a skeleton holding it out to you.

fail.log: The grottoes turn you round and round and put you out on the cloud sea at dusk, empty-handed.

choices.text: Map the isle for the Jade Court

effects.log: Your map is the first good one. The Court pays you in stones and gratitude.

events.text: The domain of a god who died before the pantheons opens its gate for one week of the heavens. Inside, the dead god's temple still stands, and its lamps are still lit.

choices.text: Walk into the dead god's temple

ok.log: On the altar is a relic of the dead god, and it lets you lift it. You feel the domain sigh.

fail.log: The lamps go out one by one as you come near. You leave before the last.

choices.text: Light a lamp for the dead god and leave

effects.log: You light a lamp and leave. On your way out the gate closes softly behind you, like a thank-you.

events.text: Mist lifts from a valley of {pw_world} that nobody has entered in sixty years. The old people say a lord of the old kingdoms buried his library there. The young people say he buried gold.

choices.text: Go in before the mist comes back

ok.log: You find the library. Most of it is mould. One book is not, and it is about you, more or less.

fail.log: The mist comes back early. You find your way out by following a stream, and lose a boot.

choices.text: Guide others in for a fee

effects.log: You guide three parties in and out safely. None of them find gold. All of them pay.

events.text: The great trading barges of the cloud sea come in from the far isles, heavy with spirit stones, star-silk and stories. Every terrace of Lantern Isle is a market for a week.

choices.text: Trade at the barges

effects.log: You trade cleverly and come away with more stones than you went with, and a bolt of star-silk.

choices.text: Listen to the bargemen's stories

effects.log: The bargemen talk about isles nobody on the inner clouds has heard of. You write it all down.

events.text: The offerings of a thousand mortal worlds arrive at the gates of the heavens all in one week, as they do every year, carried up by the spirits of the roads. The gods trade them among themselves like merchants.

choices.text: Trade offerings with the other gods

effects.log: You trade well. Your domain will eat better this year, and so will two others, who now owe you.

choices.text: Give your best offerings away

effects.log: You give them to a small god of a poor domain. That god will never forget it.

events.text: The great caravans come in from the far kingdoms of {pw_world}, heavy with cloth, dyes and stories. Every inn of {pw_kingdom} is full, and every stable.

choices.text: Trade with the caravans

effects.log: You trade cleverly and come away with more than you went with.

choices.text: Ride a day with a caravan

effects.log: You ride a day out and a day back, and learn the names of seven roads.

events.text: Old feuds wake between the factions of the isles. Banners go up on the high terraces, the Jade Void against the Nine Clouds, and the small isles choose a side or drift away.

choices.text: Carry a banner for your side

ok.log: Your banner is the last one standing on the terrace at dusk. Both sides remember it.

fail.log: Your banner goes down, and you with it, and you are carried off the terrace under it.

choices.text: Broker a truce on a neutral isle

effects.log: Nobody likes your truce. Everybody keeps it. That is what truces are for.

events.text: The pantheons raise their banners against each other over an old insult nobody remembers clearly. {b10_pantheon} calls its gods to the field of the heavens.

choices.text: Take the field with {b10_pantheon}

ok.log: The field is yours by dusk. The other pantheon sends a gift and an apology, which is unheard of.

fail.log: The field is lost, but not because of you. The gods of {b10_pantheon} say so loudly.

choices.text: Ask the Heavenly Court to judge the insult

effects.log: The Court judges it. Nobody is satisfied. Nobody dies, either.

events.text: The schools of {pw_world} raise their banners against each other this season over an old quarrel. Every courtyard in {pw_kingdom} is choosing a side, and the small schools are choosing quickly.

choices.text: Carry a banner for a school you like

ok.log: Your banner is the last up at dusk. Both schools want you after that.

fail.log: Your banner goes down in the first rush. Somebody helps you up. You never learn who.

choices.text: Make peace between two small schools

effects.log: They have been quarrelling over a well for forty years. You dig them a second well.

events.text: The immortals of the isles keep their own season of ancestors: they light lamps for the lives they lived below, the ones before the clouds. The cloud sea glows with them for a week.

choices.text: Light a lamp for every life you remember

effects.log: You light more lamps than your neighbours, and stay up all night with them.

choices.text: Light one lamp, for the life just past

effects.log: One lamp, burning a long time. You tell it everything.

events.text: In the season of ancestors, mortals of a thousand worlds burn incense to the dead, and some of it rises to the gods. You find in it the names of people you once knew, below, as a mortal.

choices.text: Answer the incense of the people you knew

effects.log: You bless every house that burned incense for someone you knew. It takes a long time. You are glad of it.

choices.text: Ask Baekun the Pale Ferryman for news of them

effects.log: Baekun tells you where each of them went, and which ones asked after you.

events.text: Lamps burn all night in the ancestral halls of {pw_kingdom}. The dead are told what the living have done, and the living are told, by the old, what the dead did.

choices.text: Tell your ancestors everything

effects.log: You tell them all of it, the good and the rest. It is easier in the dark.

choices.text: Ask the oldest person in the hall a question

effects.log: The oldest person in the hall tells you a story about the world when it was young. It sounds very like a god at work.

events.text: Stars fall over the isles every night this season, and the immortals say each one is looking for someone. The seers of the Star Sea Pavilion sit up on their roofs with nets made of their own hair.

choices.text: Catch a falling star

ok.log: One comes down slowly into your hands and goes out like a coal. In the morning it is a shard of star iron, warm.

fail.log: It comes down three isles away. You get there in time to see a crane take it.

choices.text: Count them with a seer

effects.log: You and a seer count four hundred and nine. The seer writes your name beside the four hundred and ninth.

events.text: Cheonho, Who Hangs the Stars, is taking down old stars this season and hanging new ones, and the old ones fall through the heavens past your hall. Each one carries the wish someone once made on it.

choices.text: Catch a star and grant its wish

effects.log: The wish is very small: a fisherman, a thousand years ago, wanting one good day. You give his line a good day.

choices.text: Help Cheonho hang a new star

effects.log: You hold the ladder. Cheonho lets you choose where the new star goes.

events.text: Stars fall over the hills of {pw_kingdom} every night this season. The old say a star finds the one it was meant for, and that the maker of the world hung each of them by hand.

choices.text: Climb the high hill to wait for one

ok.log: One lands, warm, at your feet. In the morning it is a black shard that hums in your palm.

fail.log: You wait all night and catch only a cold.

choices.text: Watch them with the village children

effects.log: You name every star you see for the children. Most of the names are made up. All of them stick.

events.text: A black cloud from the Demon Realm drifts up through the lower isles, and a hamlet of pill-farmers on a small isle wakes to find it in their orchards. The Ministries' marshals are three isles away.

choices.text: Clear the orchard yourself

ok.log: The cloud goes back down with a hole in it. The pill-farmers bring you their best pills for a month.

fail.log: You clear it, at a price your lungs remember.

choices.text: Fly to fetch the marshals

effects.log: The marshals come, late and furious. The orchard is saved. The marshals note your name, kindly.

events.text: A fallen god's worshippers have built a shrine of black stone at the edge of {b10_domain}, and some of your own worshippers have started leaving offerings at it, at night, ashamed.

choices.text: Break the black shrine

effects.log: You break it with one hand. Your worshippers come home, and do not meet your eye for a while.

choices.text: Ask your worshippers why

effects.log: They tell you. They were afraid. You answer the fear instead, and the black shrine falls on its own.

events.text: Grey hoods are in every inn of the river towns this week. A runner of the Shadow Lodges leaves a mark on your door in chalk, and the neighbours stop greeting you.

choices.text: Wash the mark off in daylight, where all can see

effects.log: You wash it off at noon with half the street watching. The next morning, three other doors are clean too.

choices.text: Follow the runner to see where it goes

effects.log: You follow the runner to a dye-works by the river, and learn which door the Lodges use.

events.text: The five factions send envoys to one isle, and the young of each are measured against each other on the terraces while the elders talk. A Jade Void elder you have never met asks you to stand for the faction's honour.

choices.text: Stand for the Jade Void's honour

ok.log: You win your bout and the Jade Void elder bows to you in front of the other four factions.

fail.log: You lose, gracefully. The elder bows anyway, a little less deeply.

choices.text: Decline, and listen to the elders instead

effects.log: You listen. You learn more about the isles in a week than in a century of terraces.

events.text: The four pantheons sit together in the hall of the Heavenly Court for the first time in an age, and old grievances are aired in public. {b10_pantheon} asks you to speak for it.

choices.text: Speak for {b10_pantheon} with care

effects.log: You speak with care. Nobody is insulted, which in that hall is a victory.

choices.text: Speak plainly

effects.log: You speak plainly. Two pantheons are insulted. One of them laughs, and invites you to dinner.

events.text: The League of Kingdoms meets at the great ford, and the champions of each kingdom are measured on the river meadow. {pw_kingdom} is one champion short.

choices.text: Stand as champion for {pw_kingdom}

ok.log: You win your bout on the meadow. The king of {pw_kingdom} sends you a horse.

fail.log: You lose, but not badly. The king sends you a smaller horse.

choices.text: Carry messages between the kings

effects.log: You carry messages for a week and learn exactly what each king thinks of the others.

events.text: A grey rot creeps through the spirit veins of the outer isles. Immortals who have not been ill in a thousand years are coughing, and the pill-masters of the Nine Clouds Palace cannot brew fast enough.

choices.text: Brew with the Nine Clouds pill-masters

effects.log: You brew until your hands shake. The rot breaks on the third week. The pill-masters write your name on a furnace.

choices.text: Seal your own isle until it passes

effects.log: Your isle stays clean. Your neighbours notice that you did not come.

events.text: Prayers are arriving soured in every domain, and the gods who drink them fall ill. Saengmo's hall is full of gods lying on pallets, and Saengmo herself has not slept in a month.

choices.text: Nurse the sick gods with Saengmo

effects.log: You nurse gods for a month. One of them is a god you have hated for an age. You nurse that one too.

choices.text: Find what is souring the prayers

effects.log: You follow the soured prayers back to a mortal world with a poisoned river, and clean the river.

events.text: A fever moves down the river towns of {pw_kingdom}. The healers are worth their weight in silver, the ferries have stopped, and a family across the lane has hung a white cloth on its door.

choices.text: Carry food to the family with the white cloth

effects.log: You leave food on the step every morning for a month. All of them live.

choices.text: Gather bitter roots for the healers

effects.log: You gather roots in the hills for three weeks. The healers save more people than they expected.

events.text: The peach trees of the Peach Isles have fruited all at once for the first time in a thousand years, and every terrace is holding a feast. An immortal you do not know presses a peach into your hand and refuses to explain.

choices.text: Eat the peach

effects.log: It tastes of the first day of a life. You feel a year younger, which is a great deal for an immortal.

choices.text: Plant the stone on your own isle

effects.log: You plant the stone. In nine hundred years you will have a tree.

events.text: Pungnyeon of the Golden Field has had such a harvest that the offerings are overflowing into every domain, including yours. Your shrines are piled to the rafters with millet, and your priests are starting to panic.

choices.text: Send the surplus to poor domains

effects.log: You send it on. Three small gods send thanks, and one sends a cake.

choices.text: Hold a feast for your worshippers

effects.log: Your worshippers feast for a week and pray, afterwards, with full stomachs and great sincerity.

events.text: The best harvest in thirty years. Markets overflow, even the Lodges are too busy eating to collect, and every village in {pw_kingdom} is throwing a feast. Somebody has entered a pumpkin in a contest.

choices.text: Enter a pumpkin of your own

effects.log: Your pumpkin takes second. The winning pumpkin is suspicious, but everyone agrees not to look into it.

choices.text: Dance until dawn

effects.log: You dance until dawn with people you will never see again. It is the best night of the year.

events.text: Someone sold a map to a fallen immortal's vault on a drifting isle. Now there are three hundred maps, and every isle of the inner clouds is being dug up by immortals who should know better.

choices.text: Buy a map, and go digging

ok.log: Your map is a fake. The isle it sends you to is not, and has a forgotten grotto with a pill in it.

fail.log: You dig for a week and find a cloud-sea crab, which pinches you.

choices.text: Find who is selling the maps

effects.log: You find the map-seller: an apprentice of the Star Sea Pavilion, paying off a debt. You keep the secret.

events.text: A map to a dead god's relics is being copied in every hall of the heavens. Even the pantheons are digging, in the old domains nobody rules, and pretending they are not.

choices.text: Dig in an old domain

ok.log: You find a relic: a cup that is always full of rain. The dead god's rain.

fail.log: You find nothing but another god digging, who is embarrassed.

choices.text: Leave the dead their relics

effects.log: You leave them. The dead god's domain grows a little greener the year after, as if grateful.

events.text: Someone sold a map to a fallen house's cellar in {pw_kingdom}. Now there are three hundred maps, and everyone in the river towns is digging up their neighbours' gardens.

choices.text: Buy a map, and dig

ok.log: Your map is a fake. The cellar it sends you to is not: a jar of old coins, and a letter.

fail.log: You dig up a neighbour's turnips and pay for them.

choices.text: Sell spades to the diggers

effects.log: You sell every spade in town. You are the only one who comes out ahead.

events.text: The marshals of the Celestial Ministries ride the isles this week, seizing unlicensed treasures. A marshal lands on your terrace with a list and a very long face.

choices.text: Show the marshal everything you hold

effects.log: The marshal reads your treasures against the list, finds nothing, and leaves a little less long-faced.

choices.text: Offer the marshal tea and talk about the list

effects.log: Over tea you learn who wrote the list and why. The marshal leaves without looking at anything.

events.text: The judges of the Heavenly Court read every god's ledger this week. A clerk of the Court arrives at your hall with your ledger under one arm, and it is thicker than you remember.

choices.text: Answer every line honestly

effects.log: It takes three days. The clerk closes the ledger and says, "Clean enough." From the Court, that is praise.

choices.text: Ask to see who wrote the thick part

effects.log: The clerk shows you. A rival god has been writing in it. The Court is very interested to learn this.

events.text: The Wardens of the roads are searching every cart and every cellar in {pw_kingdom} this week. The Lodges have gone quiet, and so has the market.

choices.text: Help the Wardens search

effects.log: You find a Lodge cellar the Wardens missed. They give you a grey sash.

choices.text: Warn an honest smuggler you know

effects.log: The smuggler is honest about everything except taxes. You warn them. They owe you.

events.text: An isle sealed under the cloud sea for ten thousand years has surfaced with its gate open. Its grottoes are full of mist, and in the mist something is humming.

choices.text: Go in and follow the humming

ok.log: The humming is an old immortal method, written on the air. You learn three lines of it before the mist closes.

fail.log: The humming leads you in circles for a day. You come out dizzy, with nothing.

choices.text: Wait at the gate for those who come out

effects.log: You help three lost immortals out of the mist. One of them is very important, and very grateful.

events.text: The domain of a god who died before the pantheons has opened its gate for a week. Inside, the sky is a colour that no domain has now.

choices.text: Walk under the old sky

ok.log: Under the old sky you understand something about your own domain that no living god could have taught you.

fail.log: The old sky does not like you. You leave with a headache that lasts a century.

choices.text: Bring back a handful of the old earth

effects.log: You plant it in your own domain. Something grows there that has not grown anywhere in an age.

events.text: Mist has lifted from a hidden valley of {pw_world} that nobody has entered in sixty years. The first people back say the trees there are older than the kingdoms.

choices.text: Go in while the mist is gone

ok.log: Under the oldest tree you find a stone with a carving of a figure looking down from the sky. It looks like someone you know.

fail.log: The mist comes back early. You follow a stream out, cold and empty-handed.

choices.text: Guide others in for a fee

effects.log: You guide three parties in and out. All of them pay; one of them pays twice.

events.text: The matchmakers of the Peach Isles are busy, and every immortal house is counting its unmatched. A matchmaker lands on your terrace with a scroll that unrolls all the way down the steps.

choices.text: Let the matchmaker read your thread

effects.log: The matchmaker reads for an hour and says, "Interesting." Three invitations arrive by crane.

choices.text: Ask whose names are on the scroll

effects.log: You read the scroll. Two of the names on it are people who have been in love with each other for four hundred years. You tell them.

events.text: The pantheons are arranging bonds between domains, and a god of {b10_pantheon} has asked, very formally, whether {b10_domain} might be interested in a feast.

choices.text: Attend the feast

effects.log: You attend, and are charming, and the god of another domain sends a gift the next morning with no note.

choices.text: Send a gift instead of yourself

effects.log: Your gift goes down well. Your absence goes down better: it makes you interesting.

events.text: The great houses of {pw_kingdom} are arranging marriages, every feast is an audition, and a matchmaker has been seen standing outside your door taking notes.

choices.text: Invite the matchmaker in

effects.log: The matchmaker takes your measurements, your stars and your opinion of turnips. Invitations follow.

choices.text: Sneak out the back for the week

effects.log: You spend the week fishing. You catch nothing, and are very happy.

events.text: First frost on the cloud sea: the mist freezes into lace overnight, and the cranes stand on it, puzzled. An old immortal on the next terrace says it happens once every nine hundred years, and that the lace can be walked on until noon.

choices.text: Walk out on the frozen mist

effects.log: You walk a long way out on the lace before it starts to sigh under you. You run back laughing.

choices.text: Gather the frost for a pill

effects.log: Frost of the cloud sea is a cold ingredient. You fill three jars before it melts.

events.text: The first frost of the year comes to {b10_domain} and your worshippers' prayers arrive cold, with chattering teeth in them. They are asking for a warm winter.

choices.text: Grant them a warm winter

effects.log: The winter is warm in {b10_domain}. The other domains notice, and some of them are jealous.

choices.text: Grant them firewood instead

effects.log: Forests drop dead branches all over the domain overnight. Your worshippers gather them, and learn something.

events.text: The first cold morning in {pw_kingdom}. Old wounds ache, the ferrymen wear two coats, and the wolves come down from the hills to the edge of the fields.

choices.text: Drive the wolves back to the hills

ok.log: The wolves go back up the hill. The shepherds bring you a cheese.

fail.log: One wolf does not go back, and you carry its tooth marks home.

choices.text: Mend the old shepherd's fence

effects.log: You mend the fence all morning. The wolves come, and look at it, and go home.

events.text: The isles hold their bouts for places at the Gathering of the Isle Young. Every terrace has a ring chalked on it, and every ring has a queue of young immortals who think they are better than they are.

choices.text: Fight in the bouts

ok.log: You win your ring and a Jade Court clerk writes your name in jade ink.

fail.log: You lose to someone who is exactly as good as they think.

choices.text: Referee a ring

effects.log: You referee fairly, which surprises the young immortals. One of them asks you to teach them.

events.text: Young gods are fighting for places at the Games of the Novice Spirits. A young god of {b10_domain}, very new and very serious, asks you to watch their bout.

choices.text: Watch, and say nothing

effects.log: You watch. They win. They look up at you afterwards, and that is enough.

choices.text: Give them one piece of advice first

effects.log: You tell them to breathe. They win, and tell everyone you taught them the secret.

events.text: Every town of {pw_kingdom} is holding bouts for places at the Games of the Kingdoms. The town square has a ring of rope, and a fishmonger is taking names.

choices.text: Give the fishmonger your name

ok.log: You win three bouts and a place at the Games. The fishmonger gives you a fish.

fail.log: You lose the second bout. The fishmonger gives you a fish anyway.

choices.text: Sell rice cakes to the crowd

effects.log: You sell out by noon.

events.text: Black-sailed cloud barges are raiding the trading barges between the isles. A merchant of Lantern Isle offers spirit stones to anyone who will ride guard on her next barge.

choices.text: Ride guard on the barge

ok.log: The black sails come, and go away again, faster. The merchant pays you double.

fail.log: The raiders take half the cargo. The merchant pays you anyway, because you kept the other half.

choices.text: Find where the raiders hide

effects.log: You follow a black sail into the mist to an isle that is not on any map. The Ministries are very interested.

events.text: Thieves are raiding the offerings on their way up to the heavens: whole boatloads of mortal prayers vanish between the worlds. {b10_domain} is short this month.

choices.text: Hunt the thieves between the worlds

effects.log: You find them: hungry little spirits of the roads. You feed them, and the prayers come through.

choices.text: Ask the Heavenly Court for an escort

effects.log: The Court sends an escort. The prayers arrive, with a bill.

events.text: Black-sailed boats are on the great river of {pw_world}. Nobody ships silver safely, and the ferrymen are charging double and praying.

choices.text: Ride a ferry as guard

ok.log: The black boats come close and see you, and turn away. The ferryman will never charge you again.

fail.log: They board. You fight them off the stern, wet to the neck.

choices.text: Learn the river pirates' signals

effects.log: You watch from the bank for a week and learn the lamp-signals. The Wardens pay well for them.

events.text: The Celestial Ministries are examining clerks this week, and the halls of the Ninth Stair are full of candidates muttering precedence under their breath. One of them is sitting on your steps, crying.

choices.text: Sit down and help them study

effects.log: You study with them until dawn. They pass, barely, and send you a scroll every year after.

choices.text: Give them a cup of tea and a kind word

effects.log: They drink the tea and go in, and come out an hour later grinning.

events.text: The Heavenly Court is examining new judges. One of the candidates is a god you once wronged, a long time ago. They see you in the gallery.

choices.text: Go down and apologise

effects.log: You apologise. It is not enough. It is a start, and they say so.

choices.text: Watch, and say nothing

effects.log: They pass. They do not look at you again. That is fair.

events.text: The kingdoms are examining clerks, and the roads to the capital of {pw_kingdom} are full of candidates with ink-stained fingers. Some of them carry more than brushes.

choices.text: Walk the road with the candidates

effects.log: You walk the road with them and keep the more dangerous ones honest. The rest are grateful.

choices.text: Copy notes for the candidates, for a fee

effects.log: You copy notes for a week. Your hand is a mess and your purse is full.

events.text: A trading barge from the far isles never arrived. Its cargo, a merchant whispers, was not star-silk: it was a sealed jar from a grotto that should have stayed shut.

choices.text: Search the cloud sea for the barge

ok.log: You find the barge drifting, empty, with the jar unopened in its hold. You give it to the Jade Court and sleep much better.

fail.log: You find the barge, and the jar, open. Whatever was in it is gone. You do not sleep for a week.

choices.text: Leave it to the Ministries

effects.log: The Ministries find it in a month. They never say what was in the jar.

events.text: The offerings of a whole mortal world failed to arrive this year. Nobody in the heavens can find the world. It is as if someone folded it up and put it in a pocket.

choices.text: Look for the lost world

effects.log: You find it, folded small inside a god's sleeve. The god says it was an accident. You unfold it carefully.

choices.text: Ask Unmyeong the Weaver to look

effects.log: Unmyeong finds it in an hour and says nothing about who had it. You can guess.

events.text: A caravan from the far kingdoms of {pw_world} never arrived in {pw_kingdom}. Its cargo was not cloth, a stable-hand whispers: it was the king's letters.

choices.text: Ride out and search the roads

ok.log: You find the caravan in a ravine, its people alive, the letters dry. The king sends for you.

fail.log: You find the ravine, but someone found it first. The letters are gone.

choices.text: Ask the Wardens what they know

effects.log: The Wardens know a great deal. They tell you some of it.

events.text: Snow falls on the isles for the first time in an age: real snow, from above, which nobody up here thought possible. The immortals stand on their terraces with their faces up, like children.

choices.text: Stand with them

effects.log: You stand with your face up until your eyebrows are white. Nobody says anything. Nobody needs to.

choices.text: Find out where it is coming from

effects.log: You fly up through the snow until you can see where it comes from. You decide not to tell anyone.

events.text: Snow falls in every domain at once, even the Fire domain, where Hwarin is very cross about it. The gods of the heavens are trying to work out who did it.

choices.text: Admit you did not do it, but wish you had

effects.log: Everyone laughs. Hwarin laughs too, eventually.

choices.text: Build a snow god of Hwarin

effects.log: You build a snow Hwarin with a very cross face. Hwarin melts it, and keeps the face.

events.text: The hill schools of {pw_world} close their gates for winter, and the passes fill with snow. Not everyone made it inside: a pupil is missing on the high road.

choices.text: Go up into the snow and look

ok.log: You find the pupil in a hollow under a pine, blue and alive, and carry them down.

fail.log: You find them, and bring them down, and lose two toes' worth of feeling for a month.

choices.text: Light a fire on the hill for them to find

effects.log: The pupil walks in out of the snow at midnight, following your fire.

events.text: The longest night comes even above the clouds. The immortals hang lamps on the edges of the isles so the world below can see them, and eat dumplings filled with peach.

choices.text: Hang a lamp for someone below

effects.log: You hang a lamp for someone you left below. Somewhere, a long way down, someone looks up.

choices.text: Make dumplings with the neighbours

effects.log: Your dumplings are terrible. Everyone eats them anyway, which is what neighbours are for.

events.text: On the longest night every mortal world prays at once, and the heavens are loud with it. Something knocks at the door of your hall that is not a prayer.

choices.text: Open the door

effects.log: It is a very old god, a god of nothing anyone remembers, asking for a place by your fire for one night. You give it.

choices.text: Ask who it is first

effects.log: It tells you its name. You have never heard it. Neither has anyone, for an age. You let it in anyway.

events.text: The longest night in {pw_kingdom}: dumplings, ancestors, lamps in every window, and something knocking at the door that nobody invited.

choices.text: Open the door

effects.log: It is a traveller, half frozen. You give them a seat by the fire and a bowl of dumplings, and they tell you a story about the world's maker.

choices.text: Call through the door first

effects.log: "Only a neighbour," says a voice. It is. They have brought more dumplings.

events.text: Every debt on the isles must be settled before the new year of the heavens, the Ministries say. A clerk arrives with a list of what you owe, and what is owed to you, and the second list is longer.

choices.text: Collect what you are owed

effects.log: You collect. It takes a week, and you lose two friends, and gain a great many stones.

choices.text: Forgive what you are owed

effects.log: You forgive it all. The isles talk about it for a century.

events.text: Before the new year of the heavens every god must settle with the Heavenly Court: prayers answered, prayers ignored. Your ledger is open on the clerk's desk.

choices.text: Answer the prayers you ignored

effects.log: You spend the last week of the year answering them. Some of them have waited a century. They are grateful anyway.

choices.text: Argue each line with the clerk

effects.log: You argue every line. The clerk enjoys it enormously. You pay half.

events.text: Every debt in {pw_kingdom} must be paid before the new year. Every one. A neighbour comes to your door with their hat in their hands.

choices.text: Lend them what they need

effects.log: You lend it. They pay you back in spring, with a jar of plums.

choices.text: Help them argue their debt down

effects.log: You go with them to the moneylender and argue for an hour. The debt shrinks by half.
